name: likert-matrix
title: Likert matrix
description: Several statements on one scale: a real table with one tab stop per row, a sticky statement column, and one card per statement on a phone.
docs: statements are the rows (id, text) and options the shared scale, first point first: a plain word is its own label and value, { value, label } keeps them apart. value maps a statement id to the chosen option value. The layout follows the width of its container, not the screen: from 36rem it is a real table with the scale as visible column headers in equal columns, each statement a row header and one point per cell; below that it is one card per statement with the scale as a vertical radio list. In the table every point is a radio named by its statement and its column, each row has one tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home and End move and choose inside it; the table scrolls inside its own frame with the statement column held in place. requireAll makes a form the grid sits in refuse to submit until every statement is answered: focus goes to the first that is not, those rows say "Choose one" in text, and an error lists them with a link to each. showErrors does the same for a submit of your own. name sends one field per statement, <name>.<statement id>. legend names the table and the list of cards, labels renames every word.
